summary: Frontend-only testing of the Canvas2D->PixiJS(WebGL) rendering migration + balance/boss-arrow fix. Full flow tested: landing -> character create -> ENTER THE LAKE -> intro dialogue -> gameplay canvas. Core gameplay loop (WASD movement, mouse-aim/click-fire, enemy spawn/approach, damage numbers, blood particles, kills, reload/mag indicator) all confirmed working with ZERO console errors/exceptions across ~5 test runs. Boss guide-arrow verified via direct engine-state injection (window.__game.bossActive): arrow correctly clamps to screen edge within world bounds, shows correct angle + 'Xm' distance text, and the tail-first pixel/ash dissolve animation plays correctly when boss enters view. Pause menu, Camp screen and Skill Tree all render correctly (no regression, untouched React UI). MAIN CONCERN: measured FPS (read directly from game engine's own telemetry, not screenshots) drops sharply during actual active combat -- from ~150-220fps at idle down to 10-12fps within ~15-25s of sustained firing/movement with multiple enemies+particles+blood-decals on screen, and kept declining rather than stabilizing. This directly contradicts the '60fps+ steady-state' requirement, though it may be partly explained by this being a headless/software-rendered (no GPU passthrough) test container rather than the main agent's real-browser measurement environment -- recommend main agent re-verify on real hardware AND review the renderer for per-frame-rebuilt-from-scratch immediate-mode Graphics cost (starfield/nebula/grid are recomputed with per-cell hash loops every single frame in _drawGround, and every enemy/gem/projectile/particle calls glow() which draws 2 extra circles each -- this scales the per-frame primitive count linearly with entity count with no batching/caching, which is inherently more CPU-expensive than the old Canvas2D path especially under software GL).

ui_bugs.issue: When a boss is active, the hud-boss-bar health bar overlaps/renders directly on top of the mission timer digits at the top of the HUD, making the timer unreadable while a boss is up. Pre-existing React HUD component (untouched this session) but worth flagging since boss encounters are now more reachable/testable via the arrow fix.

integration_issues.issue: FPS (read from window.__game.fps, not screenshots) drops from ~150-220 at idle to 10-12fps after ~15-25s of continuous firing+movement with enemies/particles/blood-decals on screen, and was still declining at test end rather than stabilizing near 60+. Verified this is NOT the documented screenshot/ReadPixels artifact (sampled purely via page.evaluate with no screenshots in between). Likely tied to immediate-mode Graphics rebuild cost of _drawGround (per-frame starfield/nebula/grid hash loops) plus per-entity glow() extra draws scaling with entity count. Could be exacerbated by this container's lack of GPU-accelerated WebGL (software rendering), but the degradation pattern (continuously worsening, not just 'low') warrants a real-hardware re-check.

issues: Background is very dark (near-black navy) in the first ~10-15s of a run before the zone-transition brightens it — matches old canvas engine's intentional design (zoneT2 ramps in after t=60s) so not a new Pixi regression, but combined with the vignette it can look close to the 'near-black with tiny lit circle' pattern the reviewer was asked to watch for. By ~t=14s+ with combat happening, visibility of player/enemies/particles was good and not overwhelming.

action_items: Investigate/optimize PixiRenderer per-frame cost under sustained combat load (batch/cache static starfield+nebula+grid into a texture instead of rebuilding via hashed loops every frame; consider reducing/simplifying glow() double-draw for high entity counts) — re-verify FPS on real GPU-accelerated hardware to confirm whether this is env-specific or a genuine regression vs the old Canvas2D engine.
Fix hud-boss-bar overlapping the mission timer text when a boss is active (low priority, pre-existing HUD, not part of this session's changes).
critical_code_review_comments: pixiRenderer.js _drawGround() recomputes the entire starfield + nebula + grid via nested loops with hash math EVERY frame for every visible grid cell — this is redone from scratch each render() call with no caching; for an immediate-mode Graphics API this is comparatively expensive vs a cached RenderTexture/Sprite background, and is the most likely single contributor to the observed FPS decay under load.

glow() helper draws 2 extra circle+fill ops per call and is invoked per-enemy, per-gem, per-projectile, per-particle every frame — cost scales linearly with active entity count with no LOD/culling for off-screen or very-small entities.

Boss arrow + dissolve state/math (updateBossArrow in engine.js, _drawBossArrow in pixiRenderer.js) is correct: verified clamped screen-edge position, correct angle/meters, and dissolve animation via direct state injection — logic looks sound.
dmg values in data.js (brute 65, charger 70, necron 90, steelbrute 105) confirmed to match the intended 2.5x balance fix.
No _id/Mongo concerns (frontend-only, no backend touched this session).
test_credentials: No auth/paywall needed for testing — save.runStarts < 3 bypasses paywall for first 3 runs (confirmed in App.js tryStartGame). Full credentials on file at /app/memory/test_credentials.md for auth/paywall flows if needed later.
seed_data_creation: None — used browser localStorage-based guest flow (character create -> TesterT1).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Full boot->gameplay flow selectors confirmed working: welcome-create -> avatar-{id} -> name-input -> create-confirm ('Begin Journey') -> welcome-fight ('ENTER THE LAKE') -> intro-dialogue (click ~6 times to skip 4 lines, some clicks just complete typing animation) -> game-canvas. window.__game exposes live engine instance useful for state injection (used successfully to sanity-check boss arrow without waiting 110s). Core mechanics (movement/shooting/damage/kills/pause/camp/skilltree) all confirmed functional with zero console errors across all runs. Main open item is the FPS-under-load finding above — next agent should try to reproduce on a run with GPU-backed browser if possible, or ask main agent whether this container is known to lack GPU passthrough for WebGL before treating it as a hard blocker.
rca_of_the_issue: FPS measured via window.__game.fps (engine's own exponentially-smoothed 1/dt telemetry) declines from >150 at idle to ~10-12 within 15-25s of sustained combat (many enemies + blood decals + particles + projectiles on screen simultaneously). Repro: enter gameplay, hold mouse-down to fire continuously while moving with WASD for 20-30s, then read window.__game.fps via page.evaluate. Root cause candidates: (1) _drawGround's per-frame from-scratch starfield/nebula/grid regeneration (no caching), (2) glow()'s doubled circle draws scaling with active entity count, (3) possible lack of GPU acceleration in this headless test container. Mitigation suggestions: cache the ground layer as a texture and only redraw on camera-cell change; reduce or batch glow draws; profile specifically on GPU-backed hardware to isolate environment vs code cause before any code changes are made.
